subject: NorthEast AZ outage — request for priority reroute & exec bridge
messages:
From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@greenfieldretail.com>
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
Cc: ops@greenfieldretail.com
Date: Tue, 10 Apr 2028 09:17:00 -0400
Subject: Production: Northeast AZ — checkout latency spike / 5xx surge

Hannah —

We’re seeing a major impact on our checkout flow starting ~08:55 ET for customers routed to the Northeast AZ region. Latency for token generation has jumped from ~150ms to 2.4s and we’re seeing ~12% 5xx on generation calls. Throughput has dropped ~35% for those shards and checkout failures are starting to surface in our logs.

This is material for our weekend sale. Can Redwood reroute traffic or provide an emergency mitigation? Our SREs can share logs — attaching a short dump from our gateway.

Attachments: greenfield_frontend_errors_20280410.log (text)

Thanks,
Alex Turner
Head of Platform
GreenField Retail
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Cc: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 10 Apr 2028 09:24:00 -04:00
Subject: Fwd: Production: Northeast AZ — checkout latency spike / 5xx surge

Forwarding Alex’s report — impact is high and customer is on a time-sensitive sale. Initial ask: can infra take an emergency cross-region reroute to us-east-2 or us-east-1 while we stabilize NE AZ?

Immediate asks (please reply ASAP with ETA):
- Can we flip routing policy for GreenField to prioritize us-east-2? (expected RTO: minutes)
- Can runtime team check for KV cache warmup or prefix caching loss in NE AZ?
- Can we scale dedicated pool + pin high-priority queue for this account temporarily?
- I’ll open an exec bridge if we need leadership sign-off for credits or priority capacity.

I’ve attached their log and a short checklist (reroute-checklist.pdf). Alex — I’ll keep you updated in the thread and we’ll propose a short maintenance window if needed.

--
Hannah Schmitt
Enterprise AE (Escalations)
Redwood Inference
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 10 Apr 2028 09:32:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Production: Northeast AZ — checkout latency spike / 5xx surge

On Tue, Apr 10, 2028 at 09:24 AM Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com> wrote:
> Forwarding Alex’s report — impact is high and customer is on a time-sensitive sale.

We see the same pattern in our telemetry: NE-AZ node group shows increased p99 latency and GPU memory pressure spikes. Early hypothesis: noisy neighbor + a degraded network path causing retransmits and higher token generation retries. Error traces attached.

Quick mitigation plan (can be executed within 10–25 minutes):
- Activate policy: route GreenField traffic preference -> us-east-2 (pin for 30m, then evaluate).
- Enable model-variant fallback to the slightly smaller quantized model for this customer (reduces memory pressure).
- Warm KV caches in target region by replaying recent prefixes (we have a small warmup job ready).
- Increase per-customer concurrency cap to absorb retries (temporary).

Commands / playbook refs I’ll run:
- routing apply --org GF-2027 --pref us-east-2 --ttl 1800
- runtime set-variant --org GF-2027 --model rdl-13q8-fallback

Attaching: runtime-traces-20280410.txt

Soojin
Senior Infra Engineer, Serving Runtime
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.com, soojin_lee@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com

Date: Tue, 10 Apr 2028 09:50:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Production: Northeast AZ — checkout latency spike / 5xx surge

Thanks team — sounds like we should treat this as P1. I’m standing up an exec bridge for 10:05 ET to loop CS, Eng Ops, and Sales leadership in case we need to pull reserved capacity or apply credits.

Hannah: please confirm the customer impact statement for bridge notes (bullet form). Alex: going to be on the bridge? If not, we’ll brief you after the switch.

Planned next steps for bridge:
- 10:05 ET: Exec bridge open (Zoom + PagerDuty escalation)
- 10:07 ET: Apply routing preference to us-east-2 (Soojin)
- 10:10 ET: Validate p95/p99 and error rates for GreenField; revert if errors increase
- 10:20 ET: Decide on dedicated pool burst (Rishi to advise)

Attachment: reroute-checklist.pdf

Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, soojin_lee@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Cc: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com, alex.turner@greenfieldretail.com
Date: Tue, 10 Apr 2028 12:46:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: NorthEast AZ outage — request for priority reroute & exec bridge

Bridge summary / final status:
- 10:05 ET: Exec bridge opened. Leadership and CS on call.
- 10:08 ET: Routing policy applied — GreenField traffic now preferring us-east-2.
- 10:14 ET: p95 latency for affected customers dropped to ~210ms, p99 ~420ms; 5xx rate down to 0.7%. Throughput recovered to ~95% of baseline.
- 10:30 ET: Warmup job completed; KV hit-rate restored for common prefixes.
- 10:35 ET: No immediate further action required; Rishi suggests keeping the priority pin for 45 minutes and monitoring.

Alex — apologies for the interruption during your sale, but routing change is live. We’ll keep monitoring and follow up with a short post-mortem (inc: suspected noisy neighbor, follow-up mitigation).

Attachments: post-bridge-telemetry.png (summary graph)

--
Hannah Schmitt

Redwood Inference
